Triage (first-touch grading): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, kept `tooling` + `domain:devx`, type Task. Rationale: premise re-verified — PR #10852 merged (`bfadf84`), so the `AGENTS.md:96-106` mirror is short by the two findUp anchor seeds today. Three drift rounds establish the class; a mirror-ratchet gate is the repo's established remedy shape and the card already specifies the two non-negotiables (both-direction self-test ablation; refuse-not-pass-empty when the fenced block cannot be located). Verification strategy is not a decision-box matter.

Dispatch notes carried from the card: the gate PR itself is dispatchable, but the AGENTS.md edit that adds the two missing seeds is governed surface — draft-only, human merge, so the PR lands in the ACCEPT-fork path and the gate will stay red until the maintainer merges the AGENTS.md half (sequence the gate to land with or after the mirror update, or ship the gate with the mirror edit in the same governed draft PR). Size/model suggestion: M; governed-surface one-block mechanical edit rides at opus per the 2026-08-20 tiering ruling, with fable-tier review at ACCEPT.

Claim: `domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_015ahemw8RcTgqtxrj15PEZx`, branch `claude/issue-10855-spellings-mirror-ratchet`.

**Dispatching as a GOVERNED PR**, taking the second of the two sequencing options triage names: *"ship the gate with the mirror edit in the same governed draft PR."*

## Premise re-verified on current `origin/main`

| reading | result |
|:---|---:|
| `findUp` occurrences in `scripts/check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` | **22** |
| `findUp` mentions in `AGENTS.md` | **0** |
| **control** — `__dirname` in `AGENTS.md` (a spelling that IS published) | **2** |

The mirror is genuinely short, and the control makes that zero a reading rather than a grep that finds nothing. Its sibling #10854 (the *instances*) landed as PR #11891 earlier tonight; this card is the *mechanism*, and triage deliberately kept them separate.

## Zone 1 — rulings

1. **One PR carrying both halves**: the gate **and** the `AGENTS.md:96-106` mirror correction. The alternative — land the gate first — ships it **red**, which this board has ruled against repeatedly today.
2. ⛔ **GOVERNED SURFACE.** `AGENTS.md` is human-merge-only (`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs:274-280`). The PR **stays draft**, requests review from `os-zhuang`, and ⛔ is **never** flipped ready, **never** armed for auto-merge, **never** queued — by the dev or by me. The maintainer merges it.
3. ⛔ **It must not be a phantom check** — the card's own non-negotiable, and the failure it would otherwise re-create one level up. Required: a self-test with ablations in **both** directions — a spelling added to the detector but not to `AGENTS.md` must **red**, and a mangled or renamed fenced block must **REFUSE**, not pass empty.
4. ⛔ **Not in scope**: widening or narrowing what the detector recognises. This is about keeping the published copy honest, nothing else.

## ⚠️ Collision — named, and it is a governed co-tenancy

**PR #11829** (`claude/issue-11819-adr-0125-record-drift`) also touches `AGENTS.md` and is itself a governed draft awaiting `os-zhuang`. The regions are disjoint — theirs is the ADR-0125 record and the Prime Directive #15 trigger; yours is the `RECOGNISED_PATH_SPELLINGS` fenced block at `:96-106`. Both land in the same reviewer's queue, who can order them.

If your branch goes `mergeable_state: dirty`: merge `origin/main` in and keep **BOTH** edits. ⛔ Never drop theirs, ⛔ never rebase or force-push a governed file.

## Why this card is worth mechanising rather than fixing a third time

Three rounds, and ⭐ **in two of them the stale sentence was the stated *reason* for a prohibition** — #10163's wrong "only two seeds" line justified "this seed may not change", and #10854's was the same shape. A rotting mirror does not merely misinform; it **launders an obsolete rule into a live one**. I saw the other end of that tonight: #10854's dev found the prohibition's stated reason false, kept the prohibition, and had to derive a *new* true reason for it.

⚠️ And one of #10854's claims was **already false before** the PR that supposedly staled it — so this is not only "code moved, docs lagged". A published claim was wrong on arrival and nothing caught it. A gate catches both.

**Model tier: opus**, per triage's suggestion and the 2026-08-20 governed-surface tiering ruling.

Implementation ACCEPTED and open as governed draft PR **#11908** (never flipped ready, never armed, never queued; review requested from @os-zhuang). Verified by content on the branch and on current `origin/main` — the full review is [on the PR](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/11908#issuecomment-5403165904).

Both halves of this card landed: the new gate `scripts/check-published-list-mirrors.mjs` asserts line-for-line **equality** between the detector's `RECOGNISED_PATH_SPELLINGS` and the block `AGENTS.md` publishes, locates that block **structurally** (heading + fence — this card's own `AGENTS.md:96-106` reference had already rotted to `:92-104` by implementation time), and **refuses rather than passing empty** on any unreadable state.

The premise re-measures **stronger** than when the card was filed: the detector now says `findUp` **23** times while `AGENTS.md` says it **0** (control: `__dirname` **2**, so the zero is a reading, not a dead grep).

⚠️ **One thing is NOT resolved and this card is not done until it is.** `AGENTS.md` is at its shrink-only line ceiling with zero headroom (961/961), so any honest repair of the mirror crosses it; the PR takes it to 969 and `check:pm-skill-ratchet` is red until the ceiling is ruled on. That is a maintainer ruling by construction — `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:66` requires it quoted verbatim in the raising PR, and `:58` requires it to have **its own card**. The dev correctly did not touch the CEILINGS map, and neither will I.

Filed as **#11910**, labelled `needs-user-decision`.

```
Blocked-by: #11910
Restart-when: the ceiling ruling lands on #11910

```

Expect this branch to go dirty on `lint.yml`, not on `AGENTS.md`.

Spin-off filed unassigned for triage: **#11909** — the same detector publishes its path spellings but nothing at all for `RECOGNISED_IMPORT_SPELLINGS`, so the escaping-**import** axis is unpublished. It is one row in the new mirror table plus a line budget that hits this same ceiling.
